summary.text: Andrew Lethlean is the Nationals candidate for Bendigo East at the 2026 Victorian election. Born and raised in Bendigo, he has run hospitality businesses there for about 25 years, among them Metro and Puggs Irish Bar, which he has operated since 2004. He was the Nationals candidate for the federal seat of Bendigo in 2025, finishing second behind Labor.

prior_roles.organisation: Metro and Puggs Irish Bar, Bendigo

priorities.text: Bendigo deserves a straight talker who will fight for this community
Cost of living and better local roads
A fairer share of state funding for Bendigo and regional Victoria
Better health care in the regions

sources.title: Bendigo East: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Andrew Lethlean, Candidate for Bendigo East, The Nationals Victoria
Candidates of the 2025 Australian federal election, Wikipedia

summary.text: Cheryl Hawken is One Nation's candidate for Bendigo East at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's candidate notes describe her as a cattle farmer and former small business owner whose earlier jobs were in administration and financial management. Her One Nation candidate page could not be read for this profile, and no other published biography was found.

sources.title: Bendigo East: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Denali Norsen is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Bendigo East at the 2026 Victorian election. A freelance photographer and filmmaker, he has lived and worked in Bendigo for about eight years. He has been a local organiser, helping to organise protests in support of Palestine and forums against racism, and campaigning for more public housing.

priorities.text: A society run for and by working-class people
Action on housing insecurity, climate change and the exploitation of workers
More public housing and public infrastructure, and cheaper food and energy
Civil rights, Aboriginal rights and public education

sources.title: Bendigo East: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Denali Norsen, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Des John is the Family First candidate for Bendigo East at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. According to his party page, his family moved to Melbourne from rural New South Wales in the early 1970s, and he married in 1978 and has six children and 17 grandchildren. He joined the Ambulance Service in 1984 and now works in patient transport, and says he is standing because he wants the Bible and Christian principles restored as the footing for public life.

prior_roles.note: His party page says he joined the Ambulance Service in 1984 and now works in patient transport; it doesn't say whether he is still with the service.

priorities.text: Making Christian principles and the Bible the foundation of Victorian public life again
Freedom of thought and freedom of speech
A society where hard work lets people save, buy a home and raise a family

summary.text: Liz Wright is standing as an independent for Bendigo East at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC's candidate notes, she works in the family violence sector, gained a 2024 graduate certificate in responding to family violence, and has worked with local organisations, schools and community groups. No other published biography was found; her campaign page is on Facebook, which was not used as a source.

summary.text: Michael Tolhurst is the Greens candidate for Bendigo East at the 2026 Victorian election. A civil engineer with Coliban Water and a member of the Australian Services Union, he grew up in Creswick and went to Melbourne for university. He was also the party's Bendigo East candidate in 2022, when his first-preference share was 8.7 per cent.

priorities.text: Easing cost-of-living pressure on local households
Better health care, more public housing and better transport for Bendigo
A campaign that gives everyone in the community a say

sources.title: Bendigo East: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Michael Tolhurst, Candidate for Bendigo East, Australian Greens
Candidates of the 2022 Victorian state election, Wikipedia

summary.text: Tim Rickwood is Labor's candidate for Bendigo East at the 2026 Victorian election, the seat held by former premier Jacinta Allan, who is retiring. He teaches at Bendigo Senior Secondary College, where he is also the student engagement coordinator. His party page says he grew up in a single-parent family and lives in Spring Gully.

priorities.text: Fairness and a fair go for families under financial pressure
Education as a path to opportunity
Keeping Bendigo a place where young people can build their lives locally

sources.title: Bendigo East: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Tim Rickwood, Labor candidate for Bendigo East, Victorian Labor
